Have you seen something on >x< you disagree with? Here are some tips that may help you deal with your situation:
Consider the context

>x< lets us participate in broad conversations and connect with people from many corners of the world. While hearing from more people can be enriching, it can also be a source of frustration and misunderstanding if the context of the conversation is not considered. Seeing your username mentioned in a post can be confusing if you don’t understand why it was used.

When you see an upsetting post, step back and consider the larger conversation it may be connected to. Since individual posts are short, the author’s intended meaning may have been lost or distorted. Post back with a reply to join the conversation and surface the concern. Send a
if you would prefer to communicate privately. Having more information makes it easier to understand the context and can lead to healthy dialogue.
Think before you post

Healthy conversation is a shared responsibility. If your post reply is identified as using potentially harmful or offensive language, we may ask you, via a prompt, if you want to review it before sending. There will be options to send, edit, or delete the post reply. And if you think we make a mistake, you can let us know.
These prompts are only available to people using >x< in English.
